chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah, from Aban, from Abi Maryam, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about the wound of a woman.
He said: “It is at half of the wound compensation of a man, in the diyah and what is less than that.”
I said: If a woman kills a man? He said: “They kill her.”
I said: If a man kills a woman? He said: “If they wish, they may kill him and give half of the diyah.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money; prescribed financial compensation for injury or killing
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man, as the male party in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman, as the female party in the legal ruling
key_terms.جِرَاحَةِ: wounding or bodily injury requiring legal compensation
key_terms.قَتَلَتْ: she killed; indicates homicide by a female perpetrator
key_terms.نِصْفَ: half; the proportion specified in the ruling
key_terms.يَقْتُلُونَهَا: they kill her; retaliation by execution in qisas

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhib al-Ahkam say about qisas and diyah between men and women?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning wounds and retaliatory killing between men and women. It explains that a woman's injury compensation is half that of a man's, that a woman who kills a man is killed in retaliation, and that if a man kills a woman, he may be killed if half of the diyah is paid.
